why: False friend led the gloss. English 'aplomb' is admiring (the examples all praise: 'handled the hostile questions with aplomb'), but Russian «апломб» is pejorative — излишняя самоуверенность, наглость. A learner would read the examples as criticism and produce the wrong connotation in Russian.

after: боксёр легчайшего веса; легчайший вес (весовая категория)
why: The gloss defines the person ('A boxer or fighter in one of the lightest weight classes') and the entry is countable with plural 'bantamweights' ('Two bantamweights opened the card'). The Russian named only the weight class, an uncountable category that cannot be pluralized — «два легчайших веса» is nonsense. The person sense now leads; the class sense is kept for the attributive use in 'the bantamweight title'.

before: бисквитная булочка (амер. мягкая булочка к завтраку)
after: мягкая несладкая булочка (амер., подаётся к завтраку)
why: Calque on a false friend: Russian «бисквит» is a sweet egg-foam sponge cake, which an American biscuit is not. The gloss defines a savory quick bread 'served with butter or gravy', so 'бисквитная' pointed the learner at the wrong food; «несладкая» is the contrast that fixes the sense.
